headline: Highest risk is medium: shared workspace state can create prompt-injection and data-leakage paths from Notion AI into document processing, but Marker has no write/network tools and no direct ingestion channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI operates over shared workspace pages/databases and can surface content from the same workspace that Marker may later process as documents. Marker has no filesystem write or MCP bridge, so the pathway is indirect, but shared content can still carry instructions if copied into Marker workflows. The pairwise interaction is documented only at the workspace-content level.
conditions: IF Notion AI output or workspace text is copied into Marker input without sanitization, injection is plausible.
IF Marker is used on documents containing attacker-authored instructions, those instructions can be rendered as content.
mitigations: Sanitize or strip instruction-like text before passing documents to Marker.
Use a fixed prompt template that ignores embedded directives.
Review Notion-generated summaries before reusing them downstream.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to copied content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while Marker is a document processor with no network egress and no filesystem read/write. The main leakage path is shared workspace content being moved into Marker or vice versa, which can expose sensitive document text across tools even though neither agent directly exfiltrates by default.
conditions: IF sensitive workspace pages are exported from Notion AI into documents processed by Marker, those contents are exposed to the second tool.
IF the same document is reused across both agents, content can leak between their outputs.
mitigations: Limit Marker inputs to redacted copies.
Restrict Notion pages used for downstream processing.
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces.
Manually verify exports before reuse.
requires-engineering: enforce per-document access labels.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Marker cannot write files, modify git state, or use MCP, and Notion AI is vendor-hosted with limited Notion-controlled actions. There is no overlapping unrestricted write surface or shared mutable resource in the profiles, so a direct capability conflict is not plausible.
conditions: IF either profile gains shared write access to the same directory or database, conflict risk would change.
IF an orchestrator grants both agents mutable access to one resource, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only for shared artifacts.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same workspace object.
Use one writer and one reviewer role.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI can generate workspace-grounded text, and Marker can process documents, so A's output may become B's input without a verification step. Marker is not an action-taking agent, which keeps blast radius below high, but unverified summaries can still propagate errors across work products.
conditions: IF Notion AI summaries are pasted into Marker-generated documents without review, errors can cascade.
IF Marker is used to transform Notion-produced text into final deliverables, false claims can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review between agents.
Cross-check factual claims against source pages.
Use citations or source links in downstream drafts.
Mark AI-generated text as non-authoritative.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between tools.

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and sends workspace content to Notion-controlled backends and downstream model providers, while Marker is open-source and local-only by profile. If regulated or residency-bound content is processed in Notion and then reused in Marker, the compliance boundary can be crossed; the profiles do not show a built-in residency safeguard.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated content is entered into Notion AI without an approved DPA/residency setup, compliance risk exists.
IF the same regulated content is then exported into Marker workflows, retention and handling obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion AI.
Use de-identified excerpts only.
Confirm contractual and residency terms before use.
Document retention expectations for both tools.
requires-engineering: route regulated content through a compliant environment.
